summary: Adds an order detail endpoint and a POST endpoint that applies the WELCOME10 discount to an order. Also adds a discount_code field to Order.

findings.title: Order detail readable by any logged-in user
findings.problem: order_detail looks up the order by pk only and never filters by owner. The sibling redeem view filters by owner=request.user.
findings.consequence: Any logged-in user can read the totals and discount codes of other users' orders. They only need to step through order ids.
findings.fix: Add owner=request.user to the get_object_or_404 lookup, as redeem does.

findings.title: Decimal multiplied by float raises TypeError
findings.problem: apply_discount multiplies self.total, a Decimal, by the float 0.9. Python raises TypeError when it multiplies a Decimal by a float.
findings.consequence: Every redeem request with the valid WELCOME10 code fails with a server error. The discount never gets applied.
findings.fix: Multiply by Decimal("0.9") and quantize the result to two decimal places.

findings.title: New discount_code field has no migration
findings.problem: The change adds the discount_code field to Order but adds no migration. orders/migrations holds only 0001_initial.py, and that file has no discount_code column.
findings.consequence: Queries on Order fail with a missing-column error once deployed. That breaks order_list, order_detail and redeem.
findings.fix: Run makemigrations for the orders app and commit the generated migration.

findings.title: Once-per-order discount check is not atomic
findings.problem: apply_discount checks discount_code on an in-memory copy, then saves a new total later. Two concurrent redeem requests can both see an empty discount_code.
findings.consequence: An order owner can send parallel requests and get the discount applied more than once.
findings.fix: Do one conditional update filtered on discount_code="" and on the expected total. Alternatively, lock the row with select_for_update inside a transaction.

findings.title: CSRF protection disabled on a session-authenticated POST
findings.problem: redeem changes order state for the logged-in session user but is exempt from CSRF checks. The project otherwise enables CsrfViewMiddleware in shop/settings.py.
findings.consequence: Any third-party site can make a logged-in user's browser redeem codes on their orders. The current impact is small, but the hole stays open as the endpoint grows.
findings.fix: Remove the csrf_exempt decorator and have clients send the CSRF token.

findings.title: New discount and view behaviour has no tests
findings.problem: The change adds apply_discount, order_detail and redeem, but no test exercises them. The repository contains no test files.
findings.consequence: Nothing catches the type error, the ownership gap or the repeat-discount rule before release.
findings.fix: Add tests for redeem with valid, invalid and repeated codes. Also test order_detail access by a user who does not own the order.
